subject: Operationalizing model-improvement opt-outs & subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natasha Cole <n.co@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question: data use and model-improvement opt-out for pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare internal signoff for the 6-week pilot, Legal and Privacy asked for a few clarifications before we execute the SOW and DPA amendment. Could you confirm the following: 

- Do BrightBridge pilot inputs/responses ever get used to improve Redwood models (or redirected to any model-improvement training pipeline) unless we explicitly opt in? We need a clear operational definition of "opt-out" beyond contract language.
- Can you provide a list of current subprocessors (systems that see raw text) and a simple CSV with locations (country) and purpose?
- Are there any cross-border transfers for processing (e.g., ingress to EU then US)? If so, how is that controlled?
- We also need an evidence bundle (SOC 2 report pointer or SOC control mapping) and a brief description of the technical enforcement for an opt-out flag.

If possible, can we get a short MAP (mutual action plan) that lists who will supply what and timelines? We want to avoid open legal questions delaying the procurement.

Best,
Elena
Elena Martin
Director, Privacy & Compliance
BrightBridge Health

--
Attachment: (none)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: data use and model-improvement opt-out for pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below and attached a short DPA redline + current subprocessors export. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Summary answers (high level)
- No-training default for pilot: By default, BrightBridge pilot data will NOT be routed to Redwood's model-improvement/training pipelines. We enforce this two ways: (1) an ingestion tag at request time ("no_model_improve": true) that marks data as opt-out, and (2) a downstream enforcement policy in the ingestion router that prevents such tagged data from entering long-term training storage or human review queues.
- Subprocessors: see attached "subprocessors-2026-11.csv" — columns: service, role, country, env_access (prod/staging), contact. Current list includes our hosting partner (us-east-1), monitoring, and support transcription vendor (US/EU).
- Cross-border: There is one occasional replication job from EU region replicas to our US logging tier for billing/metrics; opt-out-tagged payloads are excluded from that replication. We can provide the architecture note.
- Evidence: Attached RB-DPA-Summary-redline.pdf (high level mapping) and pointer to our SOC 2 auditor contact.

Proposed contract clause (suggested insertion into amendment)
"Customer Data flagged with the 'no_model_improve' metadata tag shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any model without Customer's express written consent. Redwood will maintain technical and administrative measures to prevent opt-out tagged data from being retained in model training stores or human review workflows."

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share the internal MAP draft (attached) and the subprocessors export.
2) Karthik and our SRE team can confirm the enforcement steps and provide a short architecture diagram.
3) If BrightBridge needs a tighter data locality control during the pilot we can discuss region locks or a dedicated ephemeral bucket.

Attachments: RB-DPA-Summary-redline.pdf; subprocessors-2026-11.csv

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

- We should include a point of contact for support escalations in the MAP (so procurement knows who to ping during onboarding).

Otherwise LGTM from Sales. I can own follow-ups on the MAP timeline with Elena once we have Karthik's note.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-24T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Question: data use and model-improvement opt-out for pilot

On Fri, Nov 21, 2026 at 11:30 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Proposed contract clause (suggested insertion into amendment)
> "Customer Data flagged with the 'no_model_improve' metadata tag shall not be used to train..."

Thanks Laura — implementation notes:
- We already have an ingestion metadata flag (no_model_improve) that flows through the router and is persisted alongside ephemeral request logs. For pilot scope we will:
  * Mark incoming pilot requests with the flag at the API gateway layer (token-level or route-level).
  * Enforce at the training ingestion job by dropping any records where no_model_improve=true. That job runs in a separate controlled cluster; we can add a unit test that asserts exclusion.
  * Block human-review queues and support sandbox access to flagged payloads via RBAC rules (neha will coordinate).
- Dataflow/replication: We'll add a filter to the EU->US replication so flagged rows are excluded; this is low-risk and we can ship within 3 working days once we sign the amendment.
- Auditability: We will produce a short sequence diagram and an exportable CSV of opt-out-tagged request IDs for the pilot window on request. That will be part of the MAP deliverables.

Drive (read-only) with diagrams and a draft runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cRB-optout-playbook

I'll coordinate with Neha on the RBAC controls and will drop a one-pager for Legal showing the unit-test and exclusion assertion.

- Karthik
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
